By consent of the learned counsel for the parties, the matter is taken up for final disposal.

This is an application for quashing the First Information Report (FIR) No. 446/2023 registered with Gadge Nagar Police Station, District Amravati for the offence punishable under Section 498A r/w. 34 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).

entities.text: Gadge Nagar Police Station, District Amravati
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 4. At the instance of report dated 31.03.2023 lodged by the informant lady, the crime has been registered against the husband, in- laws and brother-in-law.
The applicant was also made accused by alleging that informant's husband had relations with her.
The informant got married with accused- Shailesh on 22.05.2021 and started to reside at her matrimonial house.
It is her case that from the month of September-2022, she was subjected to physical as well as mental harassment at the instance of her husband and in-laws.
The informant stated some instances as to how her husband was physically harassed her.
5. As regards to the applicant, informant alleges that her husband is having illicit relation with her.
Particularly, she stated that once the applicant telephonically stated to her that she has married with informant's husband, he is not willing to stay with the informant hence, she should leave him.
On the basis of said report, the aforesaid crime has been registered.
This application is moved only by Punam (accused no. 5), who is in illicit relations with the husband of the informant.

Shri A. S. Mardikar, learned Senior Advocate for the applicant heavily relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in the case of U. Suvetha Vs. State by Inspector of Police [ 2009 (6) SCC 757] to contend that by any stretch of imagination, girlfriend or even concubine cannot be termed as a "relative" within the meaning of Section 498A of the IPC.

entities.text: U. Suvetha Vs. State by Inspector of Police [ 2009 (6) SCC 757]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Moreover, our attention has been invited to the decision of this Court in the case of Abdul Salim Ahmad Abdul Jabbar and another Vs. State of Maharashtra and another [Criminal Application (APL) No. 1054/2022, decided on 12.07.2023],
wherein this Court, by placing reliance on the aforesaid decision as well as other two decisions, took a view that criminal law is to be strictly construed and the distant relatives cannot be termed as relative in this context.

entities.text: Abdul Salim Ahmad Abdul Jabbar and another Vs. State of Maharashtra and another [Criminal Application (APL) No. 1054/2022
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In case of U. Suvetha (supra), it has been observed that the word "relative" is is to be understood for the relations with blood, marriage or adaption.
It has been ruled that girlfriend or concubine cannot find place in the statutory requirement.
Undisputedly, FIR nowhere says that the applicant was in any sort of relationship with the husband of the informant.
On the contrary it says that applicant is relative of the informant herself.
7. Be that as it may, the learned counsel for the informant submits that there is relationship between husband- Shailesh and applicant- Punam.
It is stated that the applicant's mother Maya is 4 904-apl-677-23j.odt cousin sister of the father of husband- Shailesh.
Now, the question falls for consideration that whether such distant relationship can be termed as "relative" within the meaning Punam Sureshrao Aundhakar vs State Of Mah.

2 of Section 498A of the IPC.
In other words, whether the term relative can be given so extended meaning to include any of the distant relative in the rigour of law.

8. The learned counsel for the informant relied upon the decision of this Court in case of Sunita Kumari W/o. Ram Sevak and others Vs. State of Maharashtra and another [Criminal Application (APL) No. 1660/2022, decided on 22.12.2022] to contend that this Court has dealt the issue in para no. 9 of the said decision holding that the term "relative" would depend upon the nature and status of person.

entities.text: Sunita Kumari W/o. Ram Sevak and others Vs. State of Maharashtra and another [Criminal Application (APL) No. 1660/2022
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, this Court was considering the status of real cousin sister of the husband.
The facts in the cited case are different than the facts of the case at hand hence, the said decision would not assist the informant in any manner.
9. Even as per the case of the informant, the applicant belongs to different family and was distant cousin sister of the husband.
Therefore, by any stretch of imagination the said relation cannot be said to be out of marriage or blood or by adoption.
Having regard to the line of decisions, the applicant cannot find place in the term "relative" of her husband within the meaning of Section 498A of the IPC.
Besides that 5 904-apl-677-23j.odt Police report only refers that the husband is having relation with the applicant- Punam.
So far as the act of the applicant is concerned, it is alleged that she conveyed that she is wife informant's husband and therefore, she should spare him.
Such allegation would not fulfill the legal requirements and therefore, continuance of prosecution amounts to abuse of the process of Court.
10. The application is allowed.

The First Information Report bearing No. 446/2023 registered with Gadge Nagar Police Station, District Amravati for the offence punishable under Sections 498A r/w.
34 of the Indian Penal Code is hereby quashed and set aside to the extent of the present applicant only.
